prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S879: Recurrent training shall be required at least annually and after major changes to the Regional Flow Platform, Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, or Flight Data Exchange.
S880: Simulation exercises shall use realistic traffic samples, weather constraints, surface congestion, airline schedule pressure, handling resource shortages, and recovery objectives to test coordinated decision making.
S881: Each exercise shall include participants from tower, ramp, airline operations, handling, airport operations, network coordination, meteorology, data governance, and system support functions when those functions are relevant to the scenario.
S882: Exercises shall cover transitions among Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, and Slot Compliance State.
S883: Simulation events shall require users to compare automated recommendations with local knowledge, document significant decisions in the Collaborative Decision Log, and explain departures from system proposals.
S884: Human factors safeguards shall include workload monitoring, clear alert prioritization, consistent terminology, confirmation steps for high impact actions, and protection against silent mode changes.
S885: Workstation layouts shall support rapid comparison between the Common Situation Display, Airport CDM Portal, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, and relevant advisory messages without forcing users to copy critical values manually.
S886: Training assessments shall verify that users can identify stale data, time synchronization problems, duplicate flights, conflicting constraints, and inappropriate automation reliance before such issues affect live operations.
S887: Post-exercise reviews shall use evidence from the Performance Analytics Warehouse and Audit Event Ledger to improve procedures, refine training materials, and confirm that human performance concerns are assigned to accountable owners.
S888: Deployment of the Regional Flow Platform shall proceed through phased increments that limit operational exposure while progressively adding airports, interfaces, and decision support functions.
S889: The first increment shall establish the core operational baseline for the Regional Flow Manager, Network Operations Liaison, Data Governance Steward, and System Support Engineer in a controlled production environment.
S890: This baseline shall include the Identity Access Service, Time Synchronization Service, Audit Event Ledger, Performance Analytics Warehouse, and Business Rules Registry before any airport is permitted to exchange operational data.
S891: Pilot airport selection shall favor locations with stable operational leadership, representative traffic complexity, available surface surveillance data, and demonstrated willingness to participate in joint procedure development.
S892: The initial pilot shall include one constrained primary airport and one less constrained regional airport so that both high-demand and routine operating patterns are exercised.
S893: Each candidate airport shall provide evidence that the Airport Duty Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airline Operations Coordinator, Ground Handling Dispatcher, and Aircraft Operator Representative have named accountable implementation contacts.
S894: Readiness Gate 1 shall confirm that governance, security approvals, user role definitions, operating hours, and support escalation paths are documented and accepted by local stakeholders.
S895: Readiness Gate 2 shall confirm that the Flight Data Exchange, Airline Interface Adapter, Surface Surveillance Adapter, and Weather Ingest Gateway can be connected without disrupting existing airport operations.
S896: Readiness Gate 3 shall confirm that local procedures have been mapped to the Airport CDM Portal, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, and Arrival Regulation Console.
S897: Readiness Gate 4 shall confirm that training, shadow operations, contingency procedures, and operational acceptance criteria have been completed before live collaborative decisions are made through the Regional Flow Platform.
S898: Interface certification shall be performed separately from operational acceptance so that technical conformance defects do not become unresolved procedural issues.
S899: Each interface shall be tested for message structure, time stamping, identity attribution, replay handling, duplicate detection, outage recovery, and rejection behavior under degraded network conditions.
S900: The Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, Gate Conflict Detector, Sector Load Monitor, North Runway Meter, and South Runway Meter shall be certified against agreed reference scenarios before they are used for operational recommendations.
S901: Certification results shall be recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log when they affect operational procedures and in the Audit Event Ledger when they affect access, configuration, or transaction traceability.
S902: Airport onboarding shall start with data discovery workshops that identify local tools, manual workarounds, unofficial spreadsheets, and locally maintained constraint registers.
S903: The migration plan shall classify each local tool as retired, retained for read-only reference, integrated through an approved interface, or replaced by a Regional Flow Platform function.
S904: No local tool shall be retired until the responsible operational owner verifies that its essential decisions, timing assumptions, and audit needs are supported in the target process.
S905: During shadow operations, local tools shall remain the authoritative source while the Regional Flow Platform produces parallel outputs for comparison by operational users.
S906: The cutover decision shall be based on measured agreement between local practice and Regional Flow Platform outputs, user confidence, defect closure, and demonstrated recovery from simulated failures.
